Body:
I dug into this locally on OpenCode Desktop 1.14.40 on Windows and found a more specific root cause.

The project edit dialog can persist/read the selected image through workspace project metadata (`workspace:project -> value.icon.override`). However, the sidebar project list does not consistently receive that value.

In the renderer bundle, the sidebar project list builds project data through `enrich(project)`. It only propagated `childStore.icon` / `base2.icon?.override`, but did not propagate `childStore.projectMeta?.icon?.override`. As a result:

- The Edit dialog can show a saved icon.
- The sidebar/project list can still show no image icon.
- After restart, icons can appear inconsistent between Edit and the sidebar.

The local patch that fixed it for me was to update `enrich(project)` so it also uses `childStore.projectMeta?.icon?.override` when building `project.icon` for the sidebar.

I also patched the Edit dialog preview to read the persisted icon from workspace storage, because in some cases `props.project.icon.override` was missing even though the storage record existed.

I published my local workaround/patcher here in case it helps reproduce or validate the fix:

https://gist.github.com/Bl0ck154/fa7d0b8cc900e6924e4f420da6bcb6fb

This is only a local `app.asar` monkey patcher, not a proper upstream fix, but it documents the exact behavior that made icons start working consistently for me.

Updated this PR to make Perplexity strictly **opt-in** instead of default — Exa remains the default backend. Force-pushed `dff2541`.

Changes vs. the previous revision:

- `flag.ts`: `OPENCODE_ENABLE_PERPLEXITY` now requires `OPENCODE_ENABLE_PERPLEXITY=1` to be set explicitly. Setting just `PERPLEXITY_API_KEY` no longer auto-enables the backend. Removed the `OPENCODE_DISABLE_PERPLEXITY` escape hatch since it's no longer needed.
- `websearch.ts`: backend-selection comment updated; selection logic itself unchanged (it already gated on the flag).
- `tools.mdx`: docs flipped — Exa listed as default, Perplexity as opt-in. Updated the "to enable" snippet accordingly.
- PR title + description updated to reflect the new behavior.

To use Perplexity now:

```bash
OPENCODE_ENABLE_PERPLEXITY=1 PERPLEXITY_API_KEY=pplx-... opencode
```

Upstream changed `websearch.ts` significantly since this branch was first pushed:

- Extracted `webSearchEnabled()` helper in `registry.ts` and added a `parallel` backend (Parallel Search via `@opencode-ai/core` flag `OPENCODE_ENABLE_PARALLEL`).
- Renamed `mcp-exa.ts` → `mcp-websearch.ts` to host both Exa and Parallel call patterns.
- Introduced `selectWebSearchProvider()` with an `OPENCODE_WEBSEARCH_PROVIDER` env override and per-session checksum routing between Exa and Parallel when both are enabled.

I integrated Perplexity into that new architecture rather than fighting it:

- Added `"perplexity"` to `WebSearchProviderSchema` and to `selectWebSearchProvider()`. **Perplexity is never picked automatically when Exa or Parallel is also enabled** — it only fires when (a) the user explicitly sets `OPENCODE_WEBSEARCH_PROVIDER=perplexity`, or (b) Perplexity is the *only* enabled backend (`OPENCODE_ENABLE_PERPLEXITY=1` with a key, and neither Exa nor Parallel enabled). This preserves "Exa stays default" exactly as agreed.
- Extended `webSearchEnabled()` to surface the websearch tool when the Perplexity flag is on.
- Added a `perplexity` branch to the internal `callProvider()` dispatcher that routes to `McpPerplexity.call` (our existing `mcp-perplexity.ts`).
- Added `"Perplexity Web Search"` to `webSearchProviderLabel()`.
- Updated the parameter snapshot to reflect that `livecrawl` and `type` are Exa-only (now also ignored under Parallel).

I'd like to work on this. The root cause is that the config schema expects the field name `environment` (in `packages/opencode/src/config/mcp.ts`), while the MCP ecosystem standard (Claude Desktop, Cursor, etc.) uses `env`. When users copy configs from these tools, the `env` field is silently ignored by the schema decoder, so no environment variables are passed to the spawned process.

Fix plan: Accept both `env` and `environment` in the Local MCP config schema, with `env` matching the MCP ecosystem convention and `environment` kept for backward compatibility.

## Real-world impact: 32K tokens just to start a session

Running OpenCode with:
- **Model**: qwen3.6-plus (via OpenCode Zen)
- **Skills**: ~60 skills installed across `~/.agents/skills/` and `~/.claude/skills/`
- **Session start**: 32,691 tokens consumed before any user message
- **Context usage**: 12% used at session start

### Breakdown

| Source | Approx tokens |
|---|---|
| Model system prompt | ~15-20K |
| Tool descriptions (60+ tools) | ~8-10K |
| Skill descriptions (60 skills) | ~4-6K |
| AGENTS.md | ~1-2K |

### The problem

I want skills available on-demand but **not paying for their descriptions every single session**. The current design forces a trade-off:

1. **Keep all skills** → pay 5-10K tokens per session for descriptions I may never use
2. **Delete unused skills** → save tokens but lose access permanently (have to reinstall)

There is no middle ground: no config to disable skills per-session, no lazy loading of the skill list, no way to have skills installed but turned off.

### Request

Implement one of:
- **Lazy-load skill descriptions** — only inject name+description when the model signals it might need one
- **Config to disable skills without deleting them** — e.g., `opencode.json` allows marking skills as inactive
- **TUI toggle** — enable/disable skills from the interface per session

This matters most for users with many skills who do not use all of them in every session.

## Need this for skills cleanup decisions

Running OpenCode with ~60 skills installed. Current design forces a trade-off:

1. Keep all skills → pay 5-10K tokens per session for descriptions I may never use
2. Delete unused skills → save tokens but lose access permanently

Without usage tracking, I cannot make data-driven decisions about which skills to keep. Had to manually audit 60 skills and guess which ones I use.

A simple `opencode stats skills` command showing usage counts per skill over time would let users:
- Identify unused skills and remove them
- Keep high-value skills
- Reinstall low-usage skills only when needed

This is essential for token optimization.

### Update: absolute paths alone are insufficient

Using absolute paths for the command (e.g., `/opt/homebrew/bin/npx`) fixes the initial `spawn ENOENT`, but the spawned process **inherits the stripped PATH**. So `npx` finds itself but then fails when it tries to spawn `node` as a child:

```
env: node: No such file or directory
```

This causes `MCP error -32000: Connection closed` for all `npx`-based servers.

**Full workaround** requires both:
1. Absolute path in `command`
2. Explicit `PATH` in `environment`:

```json
"notion-work": {
  "type": "local",
  "command": ["/opt/homebrew/bin/npx", "-y", "@notionhq/notion-mcp-server"],
  "environment": {
    "PATH": "/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin:/usr/sbin:/sbin",
    "NOTION_TOKEN": "..."
  },
  "enabled": true
}
```

This is a significant UX regression — previously neither was needed.

I'm hitting this same issue — my IdP rejects the authorization request because no scopes are passed on to the request.

The config scope flows correctly into McpOAuthProvider here:
`packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts L191-L196` (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/mcp/index.ts#L191-L196):
```typescript
{
  clientId: oauthConfig?.clientId,
  clientSecret: oauthConfig?.clientSecret,
  scope: oauthConfig?.scope,
  redirectUri: oauthConfig?.redirectUri,
}
```
But `clientMetadata` in `packages/opencode/src/mcp/oauth-provider.ts L38-L47` (https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/opencode/src/mcp/oauth-provider.ts#L38-L47) never uses this.config.scope:
```typescript
get clientMetadata(): OAuthClientMetadata {
  return {
    redirect_uris: [this.redirectUrl],
    client_name: "OpenCode",
    client_uri: "https://opencode.ai",
    grant_types: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
    response_types: ["code"],
    token_endpoint_auth_method: this.config.clientSecret ? "client_secret_post" : "none",
  }
}
```
The MCP SDK uses `provider.clientMetadata.scope` as a fallback when no scope comes from `WWW-Authenticate` or protected resource metadata. Adding one line fixes it:
```typescript
get clientMetadata(): OAuthClientMetadata {
  return {
    redirect_uris: [this.redirectUrl],
    client_name: "OpenCode",
    client_uri: "https://opencode.ai",
    grant_types: ["authorization_code", "refresh_token"],
    response_types: ["code"],
    token_endpoint_auth_method: this.config.clientSecret ? "client_secret_post" : "none",
    ...(this.config.scope ? { scope: this.config.scope } : {}),
  }
}
```
